g.text: Unprocessed or minimally processed food. Clean whole food source.
Active probiotic live cultures support gut microbiome
Zero added sugars, zero saturated fat, low sodium
Nutrient-dense clean staple suitable for vegetarian and gluten-free diets.

g.text: Understand food processing, chemical additives, and health impacts.
Developed at the University of Sao Paulo, NOVA categorizes all foods by degree of processing.
Whole grains, rolled oats, fresh fruits, vegetables, plain milk, eggs, and raw seeds.
Impact: Optimal nutrient density and highest health rating.
Substances derived from nature: olive oil, butter, table sugar, and sea salt.
Impact: Safe when used in balanced home cooking.
Foods made by adding salt, sugar, or oil to whole foods (e.g. canned beans, cheeses).
Impact: Balanced; monitor sodium and added sugar totals.
Industrial formulations with emulsifiers, colors, artificial sweeteners, and preservatives.
Impact: Linked to metabolic disruption and inflammatory risk.
Industrial substances frequently flagged in packaged consumer foods.

text.tspan: Used to blend immiscible liquids and extend shelf life.
Studies suggest high intake can thin gut mucosal barriers.
Industrial liquid sweetener with rapid hepatic uptake,
strongly associated with elevated triglycerides and fatty liver.
